title: K-th Smallest Pair Distance
description:
The distance of a pair of indices i < j is |ai - aj|. Among all n(n-1)/2 pairs, print the k-th smallest distance (pairs with equal distance are all counted separately).

With n = 5·104 there are over 109 pairs, so listing them is hopeless. Binary search on the answer D and count pairs with distance ≤ D in near-linear time.

Constraints

  • 2 ≤ n ≤ 5·104
  • 0 ≤ ai ≤ 106
  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n(n-1)/2

Input

Line 1: n k. Line 2: n integers.

Output

The k-th smallest pair distance.

Example

Input:

3 1
1 3 1

Output:

0
solution:
import sys
from bisect import bisect_right
from itertools import repeat
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, k = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    a = sorted(map(int, d[2:2 + n]))
    lo, hi = 0, a[-1] - a[0]
    base = n * (n + 1) // 2
    while lo < hi:
        m = (lo + hi) // 2
        c = sum(map(bisect_right, repeat(a, n), [x + m for x in a])) - base
        if c >= k:
            hi = m
        else:
            lo = m + 1
    print(lo)
main()

title: Fewest Refueling Stops
description:
A car drives east from position 0 to a target at position target. It burns one litre per kilometre and starts with startFuel litres; the tank has no capacity limit. Along the road there are n fuel stations; station i is at position posi and holds fueli litres. When the car stops at a station it takes all of that station's fuel. Reaching a station or the target with exactly 0 litres left is fine.

Print the minimum number of stops needed to reach the target, or -1 if it is impossible. An O(n2) DP is too slow for n = 105.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ target, startFuel ≤ 109
  • 0 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 0 < pos1 < pos2 < ... < posn < target
  • 1 ≤ fueli ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: target startFuel n. Next n lines: pos fuel.

Output

The minimum number of stops, or -1.

Example

Input:

100 10 4
10 60
20 30
30 30
60 40

Output:

2
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    target, fuel, n = int(d[0]), int(d[1]), int(d[2])
    st = [(int(d[3 + 2 * i]), int(d[4 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n)]
    st.append((target, 0))
    h = []
    stops = 0
    for pos, f in st:
        while fuel < pos and h:
            fuel -= heapq.heappop(h)
            stops += 1
        if fuel < pos:
            print(-1)
            return
        heapq.heappush(h, -f)
    print(stops)
main()

title: Venture Capital Ladder
description:
A start-up begins with capital W. There are n projects; project i can only be started if the current capital is at least ci, and after finishing it the capital grows by its profit pi (the required capital is not spent). Projects are done one at a time, each at most once, and at most k projects can be completed.

Print the maximum possible final capital. Trying projects in all orders or rescanning the whole list after every project (O(nk)) is too slow.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 0 ≤ W, pi, ci ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n k W. Next n lines: p c (profit, then required capital).

Output

The maximum final capital.

Example

Input:

3 2 0
1 0
2 1
3 1

Output:

4
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, k, W = int(d[0]), int(d[1]), int(d[2])
    pr = sorted((int(d[4 + 2 * i]), int(d[3 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n))
    h = []
    i = 0
    for _ in range(k):
        while i < n and pr[i][0] <= W:
            heapq.heappush(h, -pr[i][1])
            i += 1
        if not h:
            break
        W -= heapq.heappop(h)
    print(W)
main()

title: Dream Team Performance
description:
There are n engineers; engineer i has speed si and efficiency ei. Choose a team of at least 1 and at most k engineers. The team's performance is (sum of their speeds) × (minimum of their efficiencies). Find the maximum performance and print it modulo 109+7 (maximise the true value first, then take the remainder).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ si ≤ 105, 1 ≤ ei ≤ 108

Input

Line 1: n k. Line 2: speeds. Line 3: efficiencies.

Output

The maximum performance modulo 1000000007.

Example

Input:

6 2
2 10 3 1 5 8
5 4 3 9 7 2

Output:

60
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, k = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    s = list(map(int, d[2:2 + n]))
    e = list(map(int, d[2 + n:2 + 2 * n]))
    eng = sorted(zip(e, s), reverse=True)
    h = []
    tot = 0
    best = 0
    for ef, sp in eng:
        heapq.heappush(h, sp)
        tot += sp
        if len(h) > k:
            tot -= heapq.heappop(h)
        if tot * ef > best:
            best = tot * ef
    print(best % 1000000007)
main()

title: Cram Before the Deadlines
description:
There are n online courses. Course i takes ti consecutive days and must be finished no later than day di. You start on day 1 and can take only one course at a time; a course taking t days started right after the previous one finishes ends t days later (the first course taken ends on day t). Courses cannot be interrupted, and you may skip any course.

Print the maximum number of courses you can complete. Durations differ, so simply taking courses by deadline or by length is wrong; and the deadlines are too large for a DP over days.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ ti, di ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: t d.

Output

The maximum number of courses.

Example

Input:

4
100 200
200 1300
1000 1250
2000 3200

Output:

3
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(d[0])
    cs = sorted((int(d[2 + 2 * i]), int(d[1 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n))
    h = []
    time = 0
    for last, t in cs:
        heapq.heappush(h, -t)
        time += t
        if time > last:
            time += heapq.heappop(h)
    print(len(h))
main()

title: Tightest Range Touching Every List
description:
You are given k lists of integers, each sorted in non-decreasing order. Find the smallest range [a, b] (integers, a ≤ b) that contains at least one number from every list. Range [a, b] is smaller than [c, d] if b - a < d - c, or if b - a == d - c and a < c. Lists may contain duplicates, and the same value may appear in several lists.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ 104; every list has at least 1 element
  • Total number of elements ≤ 105
  • -109 ≤ values ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: k. Next k lines: len v1 v2 ... vlen.

Output

Two integers a b.

Example

Input:

3
5 4 10 15 24 26
4 0 9 12 20
4 5 18 22 30

Output:

20 24
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    k = int(d[0])
    items = []
    p = 1
    for i in range(k):
        ln = int(d[p]); p += 1
        items.extend((int(v), i) for v in d[p:p + ln])
        p += ln
    items.sort()
    cnt = [0] * k
    have = 0
    l = 0
    ba, bb = None, None
    for v, i in items:
        if cnt[i] == 0:
            have += 1
        cnt[i] += 1
        if have == k:
            while cnt[items[l][1]] > 1:
                cnt[items[l][1]] -= 1
                l += 1
            a = items[l][0]
            if ba is None or v - a < bb - ba or (v - a == bb - ba and a < ba):
                ba, bb = a, v
    print(ba, bb)
main()

title: City Skyline Checksum
description:
Each building is a rectangle on flat ground: it covers L ≤ x < R and has height H. The skyline is the outline of the union of all buildings, described by its key points (x, h): sorted by x, the skyline height becomes h at x and stays there until the next key point. A key point is produced exactly where the height changes, so no two consecutive key points have the same height, and the last key point always has h = 0. Buildings may touch or overlap.

The skyline can have up to 2·105 points, so instead of printing it, print three numbers: the number of key points K, the total area under the skyline, and the checksum C = (∑i=1..K (i·xi + hi)) mod 1000000007, where (xi, hi) is the i-th key point (1-based).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 0 ≤ L < R ≤ 109, 1 ≤ H ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: L R H.

Output

Three lines: K, the area (exact integer), and C.

Example

Input:

5
2 9 10
3 7 15
5 12 12
15 20 10
19 24 8

Output:

7
212
495

In the example the key points are (2,10) (3,15) (7,12) (12,0) (15,10) (20,8) (24,0).

title: Sliding Tile Marathon
description:
The 8-puzzle is a 3×3 board with tiles 1-8 and one blank (written as 0). A move slides a tile that is horizontally or vertically adjacent to the blank into the blank. The goal board is

1 2 3
4 5 6
7 8 0

Answer t independent queries: for each starting board, print the minimum number of moves to reach the goal, or -1 if it is unreachable. Running a separate search for every query is far too slow when t = 1500; note that only 181440 boards are reachable from the goal.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ t ≤ 1500
  • Each board is a permutation of 0..8

Input

Line 1: t. Next t lines: 9 digits separated by spaces, the board in row-major order.

Output

One line per query: the minimum number of moves, or -1.

Example

Input:

3
1 2 3 4 5 6 0 7 8
1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 0
2 1 3 4 5 6 7 8 0

Output:

2
0
-1
solution:
import sys
from collections import deque
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.read().split()
    t = int(d[0])
    qs = ["".join(d[1 + 9 * i:10 + 9 * i]) for i in range(t)]
    adj = [[1, 3], [0, 2, 4], [1, 5], [0, 4, 6], [1, 3, 5, 7], [2, 4, 8], [3, 7], [4, 6, 8], [5, 7]]
    goal = "123456780"
    dist = {goal: 0}
    q = deque([(goal, 8)])
    pop, app = q.popleft, q.append
    while q:
        s, z = pop()
        nd = dist[s] + 1
        for p in adj[z]:
            if z < p:
                u = s[:z] + s[p] + s[z + 1:p] + s[z] + s[p + 1:]
            else:
                u = s[:p] + s[z] + s[p + 1:z] + s[p] + s[z + 1:]
            if u not in dist:
                dist[u] = nd
                app((u, p))
    print("\n".join(str(dist.get(s, -1)) for s in qs))
main()

title: Fair Pay Crew
description:
There are n workers; worker i has quality qi and minimum wage expectation wi. You must hire exactly k workers and pay them (real amounts) so that

  • every hired worker gets at least their minimum wage, and
  • pay is proportional to quality: within the crew, payi/qi is the same for everybody.

Print the minimum total pay exactly, as an irreducible fraction p/q (print q even when it is 1). Floating-point arithmetic is not precise enough to choose between candidates here.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ qi, wi ≤ 104

Input

Line 1: n k. Next n lines: q w.

Output

The minimum total pay as p/q with gcd(p, q) = 1.

Example

Input:

3 2
10 70
20 50
5 30

Output:

105/1
solution:
import sys, heapq
from math import gcd
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, k = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    ws = [(int(d[3 + 2 * i]), int(d[2 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n)]  # (wage, quality)
    ws.sort(key=lambda t: t[0] / t[1])
    h = []
    sq = 0
    bn, bd = None, None
    for w, q in ws:
        heapq.heappush(h, -q)
        sq += q
        if len(h) > k:
            sq += heapq.heappop(h)
        if len(h) == k:
            num, den = w * sq, q
            if bn is None or num * bd < bn * den:
                bn, bd = num, den
    g = gcd(bn, bd)
    print(f"{bn // g}/{bd // g}")
main()

title: K-th Smallest Signed Product
description:
Given two sorted arrays A (length n) and B (length m) whose values may be negative, zero or positive, consider all n·m products A[i]·B[j]. Print the k-th smallest of them (1-based, duplicates counted).

Generating all products is far too slow. Binary search on the value; counting products ≤ x needs care for negative factors (the inequality flips) and for zeros, and integer division must round in the right direction.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 2·104
  • -105 ≤ A[i], B[j] ≤ 105; both arrays are sorted in non-decreasing order
  • 1 ≤ k ≤ n·m

Input

Line 1: n m k. Line 2: array A. Line 3: array B.

Output

The k-th smallest product.

Example

Input:

2 2 2
2 5
3 4

Output:

8
solution:
import sys
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right
from itertools import repeat
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, m, k = int(d[0]), int(d[1]), int(d[2])
    A = list(map(int, d[3:3 + n]))
    B = list(map(int, d[3 + n:3 + n + m]))
    pos = [a for a in A if a > 0]
    neg = [a for a in A if a < 0]
    z = n - len(pos) - len(neg)
    nn = len(neg)
    def cnt(x):
        c = z * m if x >= 0 else 0
        c += sum(map(bisect_right, repeat(B, len(pos)), [x // a for a in pos]))
        c += m * nn - sum(map(bisect_left, repeat(B, nn), [-((-x) // a) for a in neg]))
        return c
    lo, hi = -10**10, 10**10
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if cnt(mid) >= k:
            hi = mid
        else:
            lo = mid + 1
    print(lo)
main()

title: Watering the Weakest Plants
description:
A row of n plants has heights a1..an. One watering chooses exactly w consecutive plants and makes each of them grow by 1. You may water at most k times. Print the maximum possible height of the shortest plant.

k can be 109, so simulating waterings one at a time is too slow. Binary search on the answer and check it greedily with a difference array.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ w ≤ n ≤ 2·104
  • 0 ≤ k ≤ 109
  • 0 ≤ ai ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n w k. Line 2: n heights.

Output

The maximum achievable minimum height.

Example

Input:

6 2 3
2 2 2 2 1 1

Output:

2
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, w, k = int(d[0]), int(d[1]), int(d[2])
    a = list(map(int, d[3:3 + n]))
    nw = n - w
    def ok(T):
        end = [0] * (n + 1)
        cur = 0
        used = 0
        for i in range(n):
            cur -= end[i]
            v = a[i] + cur
            if v < T:
                dd = T - v
                used += dd
                if used > k:
                    return False
                cur += dd
                s = i if i < nw else nw
                end[s + w] += dd
        return True

title: Merge Archives k at a Time
description:
You have n archive files with given sizes. In one operation you choose between 2 and k files (any of them, not only neighbours) and merge them into one file whose size is their sum; the operation costs that sum. Print the minimum total cost to end with a single file (0 if n = 1).

Greedily merging the k smallest files every time is not always optimal: think about how many files the first merge should take.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 2 ≤ k ≤ 105 (k may exceed n)
  • 1 ≤ size ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n k. Line 2: n sizes.

Output

The minimum total cost.

Example

Input:

4 3
1 2 3 4

Output:

13
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, k = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    h = list(map(int, d[2:2 + n]))
    if n == 1:
        print(0)
        return
    pad = (k - 1 - (n - 1) % (k - 1)) % (k - 1)
    h += [0] * pad
    heapq.heapify(h)
    cost = 0
    pop, push = heapq.heappop, heapq.heappush
    while len(h) > 1:
        s = 0
        for _ in range(k):
            s += pop(h)
        cost += s
        push(h, s)
    print(cost)
main()

title: Festival Event Hopping
description:
A festival has n events. Event i runs every day from day si to day ei (inclusive), and attending it takes one whole day: you pick any single day d with si ≤ d ≤ ei. You can attend at most one event per day and each event at most once. Print the maximum number of events you can attend.

Days go up to 109, so you cannot loop over every day; sorting by end day alone is also wrong.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ si ≤ ei ≤ 109

Input

Line 1: n. Next n lines: s e.

Output

The maximum number of events.

Example

Input:

3
1 2
2 3
3 4

Output:

3
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(d[0])
    ev = sorted((int(d[1 + 2 * i]), int(d[2 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n))
    h = []
    i = 0
    day = 0
    ans = 0
    pop, push = heapq.heappop, heapq.heappush
    while i < n or h:
        if not h:
            day = max(day, ev[i][0])
        while i < n and ev[i][0] <= day:
            push(h, ev[i][1])
            i += 1
        while h and h[0] < day:
            pop(h)
        if h:
            pop(h)
            ans += 1
            day += 1
    print(ans)
main()
